extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), commanders, and installation PA staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance (AR 360-1) covering Army public affairs activities: observances, media relations, travel, support to events/organizations, productions, privacy, environmental and other PA-impacting policies. Intended to direct PAOs and commanders on allowable actions and required approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observance of the Army birthday
rubrics_metrics.description: June 14 is observed as the anniversary of the founding of the U.S. Army as the Continental Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on public events in this regulation applies to observance of the Army birthday. Commanders at all levels are encouraged to remind their personnel of traditions by reading the Resolution of the Continental Congress at troop formations (see app G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Armed Forces Day (AFD) and Veterans Day support
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD policy provides military support for Armed Forces Day and Veterans Day observances at communities designated as official DOD regional sites and for smaller local observances as resources permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AFD is the third Saturday of May; Armed Forces Week includes preceding six days. Major ACOMs may approve military flyovers for AFD and Veterans Day when within 7 calendar days of holiday. Special AFD commemorative editions of unit/installation newspapers may be published and include commander messages and features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential wreath-laying ceremonies
rubrics_metrics.description: OASD(PA) policy governs placing presidential wreaths at tombs/resting places of former U.S. presidents; Army elements at appendix H develop ceremonies and provide a Presidential representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General officer is the minimum military rank for the designated Presidential representative except when practical considerations preclude availability. Army elements must provide OCPA with name, rank, title, address, and telephone of representative on a continuing basis per table 8–1 (quarterly reporting schedule). A sample ceremony format/diagram is at appendix H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house definition and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An open house is a military program on an installation/facility to which the general public is invited to present military missions, equipment, facilities, and personnel and to maintain cordial relationships with civilian communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open houses may coincide with AFD, Army birthday, branch birthdays, anniversaries, community events, or media day. Commanders are encouraged to hold at least one open house annually within resource/operational limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house displays and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Open house displays, events, and attractions should come from host installation or local community resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: military equipment/personnel may be invited from other installations to demonstrate capabilities not found locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house audience participation and family focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Open houses, demonstrations, displays, and traveling exhibits should encourage attendance/participation by family groups; spectator participation events appealing to children are considered proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper examples include vehicle rides, junior jump towers, vision devices, communications equipment, physical fitness skills, and first aid techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house prohibited violent demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discretion is used for spectator participation events related to violent aspects of combat training; certain events are improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper events include, but are not limited to: (1) simulated or electronic weapons firing or handling; (2) grenade throwing; (3) bayonet training; (4) hand-to-hand combat demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house fundraising and sponsor restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Military open house programs are primarily PA activities and not intended as MWR fund-raising events; commercial sponsors must follow MWR event guidelines (AR 215–1, chap 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial sponsors may not restrict public viewing of aerial activities. MWR involvement permitted as long as fund-raising is not the primary objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house charges and fees prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No charges or fees for admission, parking, or viewing any activities will be imposed on the general public by the military installation or its agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installations may provide special seating for distinguished visitors at no charge. Programs containing advertising may be sold but a schedule of activities must be available at no cost. Charges for admission to military aircraft or equipment are specifically prohibited. Selling photos of attendees in military equipment or seated in military equipment is prohibited. Installations may not impose unreasonable restrictions to encourage purchases (e.g., bans on coolers or lawn chairs to stimulate sales).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ARNG armories and Reserve centers for open houses
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum use of ARNG armories and USAR/Air Force Reserve centers for open houses, exhibits, and other public programs should be encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to state governors' inaugural activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint military Service support to state governors’ inaugural ceremonies and parades is appropriate, subject to availability of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no troops/resources are stationed in a state, report to OCPA for resolution. Bands, troops, and equipment from outside the local area may be provided only if no additional cost to the Federal Government (unless approved by OASD (PA)). Support should be limited in size/scope. ARNG may be ordered to state duty by state authority; duties performed by ARNG/Air National Guard in Federal status will conform to policy. Military aviation flyovers by ARNG authorized when flown with a scheduled training mission at no additional expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Civilian Orientation Conference (JCOC) nominee criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: JCOC participants are approximately 60 influential professional and civic leaders expected to share their experiences; nominees must be influential leaders and must not possess extensive DOD knowledge or existing strong relationships with senior military members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ineligible: prior participants, partisan public officials, political candidates, persons engaged in paid partisan activities, persons (working or retired) drawing any Federal paycheck, or salaried employees of Government contractors whose primary duties are military-related.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hometown News Service (HNS) submission and support
rubrics_metrics.description: The HNS provides releases about Army and Air Force people to hometown media; final approval/release authority is the Director, Hometown News.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders should support HNS by providing suitable, timely information; encourage DD Form 2266 completion or interviews; notify HNS quickly of status changes (death, arrest, change in marital status or addresses); meet Privacy Act requirements where DD Form 2266 originates; send completed forms with supporting material/photos; verify DD Form 2266 completed more than 30 days before or after an event by signing item 21; package forms and include project ID phrases for mass submissions; consolidate forms by MOS for schools; send releases electronically when possible. ARNGUS/USAR and civilian employees, ROTC and USMA cadets are eligible per guidance. Requests for field news teams should be sent to AF News Agency/HNS at least 30 days in advance (not required for unforeseen events); field team per diem/travel costs borne by HNS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to non-Government authors/producers of documentaries/entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Army installations may assist non-US Government authors/producers without HQDA approval when subject matter is local and distribution will be only within the command's local area; regional/national interest or wider distribution requires forwarding requests to OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support provided only when cooperation will benefit DA and DOD or is in the national interest. Product requirements: (1) must be authentic in portrayal of persons/places/operations/historical events or, if fictional, depict military life plausibly; (2) must foster improved understanding of the Army and DOD; (3) cannot appear to condone or endorse activities contrary to US Government policy or not in best interest of Army/DOD. OCPA–LA processes requests for film/TV/multimedia; PAOs should request OCPA–LA guide. Appearances by Army personnel in official capacity or in uniform must be approved based on level of interest. Talk show participation with regional/national interest requires OCPA approval. Participation/support must be unique in character, must not have a commercial counterpart, must not benefit DA and DOD, and must be in the national interest. Promotional assistance to publishers/producers submitted to OCPA. Army policy prohibits using Army themes/material/uniforms/insignia in advertisements/promotions that could imply Army endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval for Army visual information productions
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual information productions made by the Army and intended primarily for public release (excluding local materials or spot news) must be approved by the OCPA and the OSD prior to committing military funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See DA Pam 25–91 for policies and procedures on producing visual information materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA responsibilities for environmental protection and NEPA actions
rubrics_metrics.description: PA responsibilities/support in connection with Army Environmental Protection and Enhancement Program are in AR 200–1; PAOs must be familiar with environmental laws including NEPA and Executive Order 12088.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should work closely with local engineers and environmental coordinators on a continuing basis and especially when conducting Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) actions (installations activations, base closures/realignments/reductions, real estate acquisition, major construction, training exercises with significant environmental damage potential, dredging, movement/actions on chemical agents/munitions). EIS processes may include public hearings of crucial interest to media/public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land acquisition public engagement and congressional notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform and engage the public about land acquisition studies thoroughly and quickly throughout the acquisition process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congressional notification must precede or coincide with public release. Close coordination among local and ACOM PAOs and the OCPA on all land acquisition actions is imperative (see AR 405–10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act and personal privacy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Privacy Act of 1974 generally prohibits the Department of the Army from publicly releasing certain items of information about an individual without that individual's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on applying the Privacy Act to PA activities is in appendix E; consult AR 340–21 and related references.

rubrics_metrics.name: References for release of information on disciplinary/criminal/investigative matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of information on disciplinary actions, criminal investigations, DA polygraph activities, and military police records are governed by referenced regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See AR 25–55 for disciplinary actions; AR 195–6 para 2–9 for polygraph activities; AR 190–45 chap 3, AR 195–2 para 4–3, AR 25–55, and AR 340–21 for release from criminal investigation and military police records; AR 381–12 and AR 381–20 for counterintelligence guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil support public affairs coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil support operations are conducted in an interagency environment with a lead Federal agency that directs civil support operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Federal Joint Information Center (JIC) will often be established by the lead agency for PA operations and information release. The senior DOD PAO in the area will coordinate with the lead agency, and DOD will usually assign PA representation to the JIC. Local PA support governed by PA guidance from U.S. Northern Command through U.S. Army Forces North.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of military transportation assets for PA travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Military transportation assets will not be used to compete with commercial carriers of U.S. registry if commercial transportation is available, adequate, and meets the PA objectives of the proposed travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA travel must be primarily in the interest of DA or DOD. No commitment of military transportation until request coordinated and approved. Orders covering transportation issued by command with primary interest. DOD must approve PA travel arranged with another Federal agency or foreign government. Travel to serve humanitarian purposes or increase goodwill alone does not meet criteria. Liability releases are required for non-DOD personnel for PA travel on military aircraft. Approval authority to use military carriers for nonlocal community relations travel for non-DOD persons rests with SECARMY (delegated to commanders grade major general and Director, NGB) and may not be further delegated. Commanders may grant approval for local travel if PA impact is confined to vicinity, transportation is for approved local PA program, and subject matter is not the responsibility of higher command. Military transportation for media representatives/authors/writers is on a space available, nonreimbursable basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local media travel procedures and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Local travel is within the command's geographic area of responsibility or PA sphere of influence; news media may be authorized travel when travel is an integral part of a story and provided on a space available basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commander in whose area the travel occurs may approve local travel for local news media representatives. All local travel/transportation for national media representatives should be brought to attention of OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonlocal media travel approval criteria and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: All nonlocal media travel requires DOD approval and will be approved only under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) travel by military transportation is integral to the story (evacuations, maneuvers, troop movement) and limited to assignment needs; (2) proposed coverage is major emergency and coverage would be impaired/delayed without military transportation — requests via fastest means to OCPA; (3) travel is of special interest to the Army and part of an approved PA project. Procedures: forward requests through command channels to OCPA; ensure requests contain dates, destinations, justification, and a point of contact who is familiar with regs/security matters; ensure media are briefed on passport/visa/immunization requirements and provided protective gear if required; submit copies/summaries of coverage after the event to OCPA. PA officers are not required or encouraged to accompany news media on nonlocal travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special travel category approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: State adjutants general may approve PA travel within their states; the NGB PA office must approve local travel to facilities outside their states/territories; other ARNG media travel requires DOD approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air transportation procedures for members of Congress and their staffs are in AR 1–20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Army aircraft for nonmedia PA travel and orientation flights
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of PA activities that may qualify for travel in Army-owned/controlled aircraft include invitational or authorized travel to support approved PA activities, tours/conferences sponsored by DA/DOD, joint tours with other agencies/governments, authors/writers covering approved programs when travel integral to story on space available basis, and guests of SECDEF/SECARMY participating in official programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approvals not provided for flights involving record attempts, first flights of aircraft just entering inventory, first flights over isolated areas, or other abnormal conditions. Army aviation assets not used to transport persons costumed as holiday characters. Orientation flights must be in suitable passenger-carrying aircraft; travelers must wear proper organizational uniforms and present ID; minors require written parental consent; orientation flights normally originate/terminate at an installation with exceptions by ACOMs case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: VIP travel information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: General information on VIP travel handled as official use only; specific VIP travel itineraries should be classified confidential for security reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph 6–3 for guidance on travel for official Army speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCPA liaison and notification requirements for organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: OCPA maintains liaison with national service-oriented organizations; support to non-Government organizations must conform to DOD 5500.7–R and this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCPA must be notified in advance of command cooperation in industry or non-Government association programs that could generate significant public interest beyond the local/regional level. OCPA periodically sends information on DA policies, programs, budgets, and other activities in response to organization requests; Major ACOMs encouraged to provide materials for these mailings (posture statements, significant statements, internal publications, policy pronouncements, speeches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership in organizations and associations rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on DA military/civilian membership or participation in private organizations is in DOD 5500.7–R and DODI 1000.15; command memberships in local civic organizations are authorized when beneficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one command membership in each organization may be purchased for the headquarters of each ACOM and installation; register membership in name of installation/command to avoid name changes due to reassignments. Normally purchased with appropriated funds; NAF expenditures allowed if membership supports morale/welfare/mission objectives and appropriated funds unavailable. Using appropriated funds to pay individual membership fees/dues prohibited by 5 USC 5946; agencies may pay for professional society memberships in the name of the agency when necessary to accomplish authorized activities. Personnel prohibited from accepting honorary office/membership in private associations whose membership includes business entities engaged in providing goods/services to a DOD component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison protocols outside National Capital area
rubrics_metrics.description: OASD(PA) is the principal point of contact for national non-Government organizations and their chapters in the National Capital area; outside that area local commanders may communicate directly with local/regional chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OASD(PA) authority does not apply to matters bearing directly on the Army, requests for speakers, contractual/consulting matters, or matters handled by scientific/technical info services of DLA. Matters pertaining to the Army as a whole or principal headquarters will be referred to OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to national military association conferences: eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: SECARMY has approval authority to provide military support to specified national military associations; OASD(PA) designates/approves specified associations eligible for support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to support associations not on approved list must be submitted in writing through channels to OCPA at least 90 days before event. Support limited to annual conference/convention (one per calendar year). Eligibility: associations must be noncommercial, national in scope, and focus efforts on active duty/ARNG/USAR activities; associations oriented primarily toward veterans or specific units/campaigns/gender/ethnic group/religion/region do not meet eligibility. Authorized support while on duty limited to duties related to designated military specialties; personnel/equipment use must be at no additional cost and logistical support must be incorporated into legitimate training missions. Examples of authorized support include limited air/ground transportation (subject to approvals and limits), limited communications support, medical assistance for emergency/lifesaving only, administrative support reasonably timed (generally no more than 2 weeks prior and 1 week after announced dates), and security support if civilian resources insufficient and documented by official requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on activities involving contractors and military-related organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting gratuities from private companies in connection with an association's activities is prohibited; Army civilian and active duty personnel are restricted from certain contractor-related hospitality/attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibitions include attending social functions as guests of any contractor/potential contractor, accepting hospitality from such contractors, and accepting invitations to association banquets/luncheons unless sponsor demonstrates in advance that (1) the affair will have open seating and (2) seating is neither selected nor influenced by contractor interests. Personnel prohibited from accepting gifts other than specialty advertising items of trivial intrinsic value. Invitations may be accepted only if sponsor assures no single contractor or industry-developed guest lists/seating plans reflect special interests.
